bug_semantics: The now-rejected report alleged that an attacker could alter the authentication strategy in an OTP-stage sign-in request and complete an OAuth sign-in without the correct code because the server did not revalidate the prepared verification stage. The public report supplies no concrete request, strategy pair, reproducible proof, or vulnerable server behavior, and the canonical CVE record now states that further investigation found this was not a security issue.
flaw_origin: If the reported behavior had been real, the security decision would have been in Clerk's Frontend API server: the server would have failed to bind an attempted factor strategy and credential to the sign-in's prepared challenge. packages/clerk-js/src/core/resources/SignIn.ts is only a typed transport wrapper that posts caller-supplied factor parameters to attempt_first_factor/attempt_second_factor; client-side typing or request construction cannot enforce authorization against a network attacker. The canonical CNA rejection means no actual flaw origin is established in this repository or elsewhere.
ai_marker: not applicable: the CNA rejected the claimed vulnerability and no smallest BIC exists, so no commit object can be inspected or attributed for BIC-only AI evidence
evidence: Canonical disposition: https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2025-63700 reports cveMetadata.state=REJECTED, dateRejected=2025-12-23, and the CNA reason verbatim: 'DO NOT USE THIS CVE RECORD... Further investigation showed that it was not a security issue.' NVD independently renders the same rejected status and reason at https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-63700. The original disclosure at https://github.com/itsnishat08/CVE-2025-63700 only describes changing one authentication strategy to another and alleged backend non-revalidation; it provides no endpoint transcript, strategy values, PoC, patch, or commit. Version check: git rev-parse @clerk/clerk-js@5.88.0^{} resolves the affected tag to c3facf1d1877261c01be5a446458f37e75c6d354 (tagged 2025-08-21); GitHub still lists <=5.88.0 and 'Patched versions: None'. Source check at that tag: packages/clerk-js/src/core/resources/SignIn.ts attemptFirstFactor and attemptSecondFactor post the supplied body to attempt_first_factor/attempt_second_factor and therefore delegate validation to FAPI. History check: blame leads those generic posting lines to 8b00a66c18924a2a99afdb3539bd6663d68eb673, 'More Clerk packages going Open Source (#20)', a 2,093-line wholesale package import. Its immediate parent 679ab0e0054250cf9269d28b097cac043ac761a1 has only backend-core, edge, and sdk-node under packages and no clerk-js tree. That aggregate is not a smallest BIC and cannot be decomposed from this public history. No fix commit or patched release exists because the issue was withdrawn as non-security; the post-boundary @clerk/clerk-js@5.89.0 tag resolves to 3cb634c4a9431a4680350351ffc1516b99e4157e, and its intervening OTP commit f871573b5546a27719a2e8f3e5529594db8828bc only rewrites the visual OTP input for autofill/password-manager compatibility, not server verification.
reasoning: Vulnerability-first reconstruction stops before AI attribution. The only described attack requires a server to accept a manipulated verification strategy without validating it against the prepared sign-in state. The JavaScript SDK merely serializes and sends that request, so its generic attempt-factor methods are not the authorization root cause. More decisively, the canonical CNA later withdrew CVE-2025-63700 after determining that it was not a security issue. Consequently there are no proven vulnerable lines, no real BIC whose parent can demonstrate flaw absence, and no security fix or patched boundary to identify. The oldest public client transport code is a wholesale open-source import rather than an atomic introducer, and treating it as the BIC would violate the smallest-BIC rule. With no BIC, inspecting that aggregate's authorship or trailers would also violate BIC-only AI attribution. A closed NOT_AI or AI verdict is therefore unsupported; EVIDENCE_GAP records that the stale GHSA/bundle claim cannot be mapped to a valid vulnerability lifecycle.
remaining_gap: No valid vulnerability mechanism, smallest BIC, parent-absence proof, or fix exists to audit: the CNA rejected CVE-2025-63700 as not a security issue, while GitHub's GHSA page remains stale. Reopening attribution would require a reproducible request/response transcript proving the claimed bypass and access to the causal FAPI server implementation/history; absent that, no BIC-only AI verdict is possible.
